steps: This video shows how prompt caching stops you paying for the same long document again and again. The legal workflow sends Claude the same eighty page filing, about forty thousand tokens, on each of fourteen queries.
Each of those queries is billed as fresh input. Fourteen times forty thousand is five hundred and sixty thousand tokens, at three dollars per million, which comes to one dollar sixty-eight per case.
So you change the prompt layout the legal workflow sends. The static filing goes first, marked with cache control set to ephemeral, and the changing question comes after it.
On query one, Claude writes the forty thousand token prefix into the prompt cache, charged at roughly input price, about twelve cents. The cache now holds it with a five minute time to live.

Queries two through fourteen send the same prefix, and Claude reads it from the cache instead. Cache reads cost thirty cents per million, about ten percent of input price, and skipping prefill lowers time to first token.

Claude returns the bill to legal: thirteen cache reads cost about sixteen cents. Per case, the filing cost falls from one dollar sixty-eight to about twenty-eight cents, an eighty-four percent saving.

Your rollout rule: cache any static prefix of at least one thousand and twenty-four tokens that is reused within five minutes. Takeaway: put stable content first and pay full price for it only once. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
